title: Tag-document linking
summary: associate every flat canonical tag with one Analysis tag document while keeping the registry description independent after one-time document seeding
content_html:
Tag-document linking

Result

Every canonical tag registry record contains one required, unique doc_id intended to identify a document in the Analysis tags sub-scope. New Tag and association replacement validate that relationship when they write it. Documents are managed independently, so later document deletion may leave a stale registry ID until the user repairs it.

The registry owns the one-way association. A document does not carry a tag_id back-reference, and documents that are not referenced by a tag remain valid. The document owns long-form meaning. The registry description remains independent concise metadata: it may seed a newly created document once, but neither side synchronizes later edits to the other.

The final registry record is:

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "group": "subject",
  "description": "<independent registry description>",
  "doc_id": "d-<immutable document ID>",
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

Relationship contract

tag registry record
  -> required unique doc_id
      -> one existing Analysis/tags document
      -> or stale after independent document deletion
  • Every registry record has exactly one nonblank doc_id.
  • A doc_id must resolve within the configured Analysis tags sub-scope when New Tag first assigns it or Edit Tag replaces it.
  • No two registry tags may reference the same document.
  • Documents contain no tag_id field and may exist without a registry reference.
  • Deleting a tag leaves its document intact and unreferenced.
  • Deleting a document does not update the tag registry. It may leave a stale doc_id that the user must replace through Edit Tag.
  • tag_id is not editable through Edit Tag.
  • Neither document title nor content is used to infer or repair an association.

One-off migration contract

The migration is driven only by flat tag registry records and their explicit document-ID field. For each tag without that field, it allocates a new immutable doc_id, creates one document in the Analysis tags sub-scope, and writes the new ID back to that registry record.

Each new document starts with:

---
doc_id: <allocated immutable document ID>
title: "<tag_id>"
added_date: <migration timestamp>
last_updated: <migration date>
parent_id: ""
viewable: true
---
# <tag_id>

**<group>**

<tag registry description>

The registry description is copied once as initial content. It remains in the registry as independent concise metadata after the created sources and associations are verified. Later registry-description edits do not update the document, and document edits do not update the registry description.

The migration explicitly chooses viewable: true because the tag documents are intended to be public. This is an outcome choice, not a technical limitation: the migration could author viewable: false, and either value could later be changed directly in source. This feature does not add a visibility control.

The completed management prerequisite makes the generated collection navigable, viewable, and source-editable. The first delivery deliberately uses the real generated set to review what further management work is justified.

The three documents already in the tags sub-scope are not inspected, matched, reused, moved, or updated by the migration. Their unique doc_id values remain their identities. Unless a registry record is linked to one separately through an explicit document ID, they remain independent documents and do not reduce the migration's create set.

The sub-scope manifest remains the existing minimal public document-list contract. It may contain hundreds of records, so this feature does not project canonical tag data into every public row. The manifest does not receive tag_id, group, groups, or registry description, and this feature adds no group filtering or styling to the report.

Ongoing creation and mutation contract

The required relationship continues after the migration:

  • New Tag must create or resolve an Analysis tags document before committing the registry row. Creating the document first is safe because unreferenced documents are allowed; committing a tag first would violate the write-time validation. When New Tag creates the document, the submitted registry description seeds its initial content once.
  • A tag edit may replace doc_id only with an existing, currently unreferenced Analysis tags document. It cannot clear the field.
  • A tag delete removes only the registry record and its assignment/alias effects already owned by the tag mutation planner; it does not delete the document.
  • Document deletion remains independent and does not consult or update the tag registry. A deleted target leaves its registry doc_id stale until the user replaces it.

The Tag Registry modal is the association inspection and navigation surface:

  • Edit Tag currently treats tag_id as non-editable identity and edits only description. This feature adds the required doc_id as a second editable field; it does not make tag_id editable.
  • The modal exposes the current document ID, including a stale ID, and can replace it within the constraints above.
  • Save persists description and doc_id independently through the ordinary tag edit mutation. Neither change updates the document.
  • The field accepts immutable Docs Viewer doc_id values for the Analysis tags sub-scope.
  • Open derives /docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=<document ID>; the URL is not stored in the registry.
  • Open is available only when the current field value resolves to a listed Analysis tags document. An invalid value shows a contained unavailable state, does not render a dead link, and remains available for replacement.
  • The modal can inspect, replace, save, and open an association. It does not edit or delete document content.

Delivery Documents

  • Tag Document Bootstrap Delivery — generate and link the current complete document set, then stop for collection-level management review.

Further tag creation, association-edit, and stale-link repair deliveries wait for that review rather than being designed into the bootstrap. Generic sub-scope collection management belongs to Sub-Scope Index.

Related Docs Viewer workflow

Dense sub-scope navigation and Markdown source editing belong to Manage Sub-Scope Documents, not this feature. That feature is a prerequisite for the migration. Tag-document linking then owns the public document creation, registry association, and public deep link.

Collection-local selection, document controls, and adoption by applicable collection functions belong to Sub-Scope Index. The Analysis tags collection is a consumer and review surface for that generic Docs Viewer feature, not its owner.

Downstream semantic-token dependency

A Tag semantic-token target cannot be registered until it can resolve to a stable, workable destination. A resolving registry doc_id association and the public subdoc URL produced by this feature provide that destination. A stale association remains unavailable until the user repairs it.

Tag token work therefore waits for this feature and its prerequisites. It must not infer or repair a target from mutable document title, description, or content, and it must not add placeholder target-lookup rows without a usable href.

Durable Destinations

The required registry link and navigation workflow belong in Tag Registry. The final source relationship belongs in Tag Source Data. Stable sub-scope list/detail behavior remains owned by Embedded Detail Documents.
